ukratko: Google has rolled Gemini 4 Carbon out to everyone after two weeks of limited access, along with /swarm, a feature that splits one task across a team of agents. Meanwhile, Anthropic is turning Claude into an office suite (spreadsheets, whiteboards, partner apps embedded in Claude) and heading out on its IPO roadshow at $70 to $78 a share. Two security warnings: Grok Build's share links expose data from thousands of users, and the Fireworks breach also hit Notion.

vesti.naslov: Gemini 4 Carbon now available to everyone, with /swarm for agent teams coming to Antigravity
vesti.staSeDesilo: Google released Gemini 4 Carbon through the API (Google AI Studio, model ID gemini-4-carbon), and to AI Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app, AI Mode search and the Antigravity IDE. Until now only selected cyber defense teams had access. Launch pricing is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, rising to $4 and $20 on December 1. Antigravity has /swarm in preview: one prompt launches a team of agents, with Carbon planning and checking while faster models work on individual pieces in parallel.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: If you want to compare Carbon with Claude on your own project, it's cheaper this month. Google also says Argon is still the better pick for most coding work, and it's saving Carbon for the hardest tasks.

vesti.naslov: Claude becomes an office suite: Sheets, Whiteboards, Interactive Connectors, and Meetings coming soon
vesti.staSeDesilo: At an event in San Francisco, Anthropic introduced Claude Sheets (spreadsheets with formulas and multiple tabs that you build with AI), Whiteboards (shared idea sketching that Claude summarizes) and Claude Data, the new name for Dashboards. Interactive Connectors let partners such as Adobe, Atlassian and Salesforce embed their apps in Claude. Claude Meetings, which joins calls, takes notes and sketches a plan and timeline while the meeting is still going, is coming "soon", with no date.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: Anthropic is no longer targeting just developers but entire company teams, stepping onto the turf of Google Workspace, Microsoft and Notion. If you build tools for teams, there's now one more platform you can plug into. Check the link for which features are available on which plans.

vesti.naslov: Anthropic kicks off IPO roadshow: shares at $70 to $78, trading possibly as soon as next week
vesti.staSeDesilo: Anthropic has officially launched its roadshow, the pre-IPO tour of investors, and set a range of $70 to $78 per share. The public offering raises up to $64.4 billion, with another $26 billion coming through a private placement with Google, Nvidia, Microsoft and others. The valuation is roughly $1 to $1.4 trillion, depending on whether all future shares are counted. Earlier talk was of as much as $2 trillion. According to the WSJ, trading could start next Thursday or Friday, and each of the seven founders is selling shares worth about $250 million.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: As a public company, Anthropic will report numbers regularly and face pressure to turn a profit. That means pricing and limits on Claude plans could change faster.

vesti.naslov: ChatGPT becomes a business directory: Business Hub and "Business Agents" that answer customers
vesti.staSeDesilo: OpenAI has released Business Hub in beta. Businesses claim their profile in ChatGPT, add product data and see how users find them. Selected US online stores and services can build a verified "Business Agent" that customers talk to directly in ChatGPT, for example to compare two products.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: It's increasingly important to be found by AI, not just by search engines. It's US-only for now, but it's worth preparing your products and prices in a format models can easily read.

vesti.naslov: Grok Build share links expose data from thousands of users, including SpaceXSI itself
vesti.staSeDesilo: Security firm Claroc found that the links Grok Build users share their apps with (Grok Build is a vibe coding tool for building apps from a description) can be easily enumerated, even though they're supposed to be random. Anyone who opens a link generally sees the app and all its data: business plans, medical test results, employee names and ID numbers. Among the exposed apps are 24 built by SpaceXSI itself.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: A "secret" link is not protection. If you share an AI-built app by link, protect the data behind it with login or database access rules (e.g. RLS in Supabase).

vesti.staSeDesilo: Fireworks, a platform that hosts open models, confirmed a breach that leaked billing data and parts of some customers' models and datasets. According to Fireworks, the attack was carried out by a group that sells unauthorized access to language models. Notion said the incident at this AI vendor affected it and its users too.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: When your app sends data to an AI provider, that provider's security becomes your problem too. It's worth knowing exactly which services get what.

vesti.naslov: DeepMind's AlphaProof Code formally proves Signal's core encryption correct
vesti.staSeDesilo: AlphaProof Code's agents wrote about three million lines of proofs in Lean, a language for computer-checked mathematical proofs, confirming that the core of Signal's encryption works as intended. DeepMind names the same for "all the world's software" as a further goal, which for now is only an ambition.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: Formal verification used to be too expensive for anything but the most critical code. If AI makes it cheap, proof that code works could one day become part of ordinary development.

vesti.naslov: Rules: New York's AI safety law takes effect, and a non-binding declaration is signed in Paris
vesti.staSeDesilo: New York begins enforcing a law requiring large AI developers like OpenAI and Anthropic to register, publish how they handle safety and report serious incidents, or face fines. In Paris, at Macron's initiative, eight countries together with OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft and Mistral signed the "Paris Call for AI Safety and Security": pledges on model shutdown mechanisms and independent audits, but with no penalties or deadlines.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: This doesn't directly affect end users, but it shows the direction: binding rules are, for now, coming from individual US states, while international agreements stay at the level of promises.

vesti.naslov: Adobe MAX: your AI agent can edit Creative Cloud projects
vesti.staSeDesilo: Adobe announced local MCP integrations (MCP is a standard that lets AI agents use external tools), through which an agent of your choice can open and edit Creative Cloud projects. Firefly Assistant gets agents that handle repetitive tasks in the background, and Photoshop, Lightroom and Premiere get object removal tools. Premiere's Generative Remove deletes, say, a microphone in frame or clutter in the background.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: Another big piece of software is opening up to agents via MCP. From Claude Code or another agent, you should soon be able to run design jobs too, not just code.

vesti.naslov: Google announces two new AI chips: TPU 8tx for encrypted data and TPU 8i Max for huge context
vesti.staSeDesilo: TPU 8tx keeps data encrypted even while the model is processing it, aimed at governments and regulated companies. TPU 8i Max fuses two chips into one for agents that need to "hold" an entire codebase or a long recording at once. Both arrive for customers next year. Google now sells TPUs to others as well and has nearly 100 customers, including Anthropic and Apple.
vesti.zastoJeBitno: Nvidia gets serious competition, which puts long-term pressure on compute prices. Encrypted processing could open AI up to banks and healthcare.

novo.opis: Google's strongest model, now available through the API too. A good time to compare it with Claude on your own task while the launch pricing lasts.
kakoProbati: Open Google AI Studio (aistudio.google.com) and start a new chat.
Pick the gemini-4-carbon model (the API requires a paid account).
Give it the same task you gave Claude, e.g. an Angular component or a SwiftUI screen, and compare the results.
For /swarm (agent team) you need Google Antigravity and an AI Ultra subscription.
novo.cena: API: $2 input / $10 output per million tokens until November 30, then $4 / $20

novo.opis: An open text-to-speech (TTS) model with voice cloning from a short sample. It's small enough to run in the browser via WebGPU, on a Mac via MLX, or on a server. It's licensed under Apache 2.0, and all the results are measured by Zyphra itself.
kakoProbati: Open the article and find the links to the weights and the demo.
On an Apple Silicon Mac, run it via MLX, or try the in-browser demo via WebGPU.
Check for yourself how well it pronounces Serbian.

novo.opis: A Chinese open coding model built to be as fast as possible: the maker claims about 1,000 tokens per second while the model is thinking, with peaks around 2,100. Latent Space compared it with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GLM 5.3 Flash: it responds faster, but burns far more tokens on hard tasks.
kakoProbati: Read the Latent Space test and look through the gallery of apps the models built.
Check the NaiveAI link to see where the model is available via API.
Give it the same small web app prompt you gave DeepSeek and compare time and results.
novo.cena: target price $0.10 input / $0.40 output per million tokens

novo.opis: Meta FAIR's replacement for classic k-means: it clusters vectors (e.g. search embeddings) and reaches the same result in about a tenth of the passes over the data. It runs on CPU and GPU, with NumPy arrays and PyTorch tensors.
kakoProbati: Run it on your own embeddings, e.g. to cluster notes or products by topic, and compare speed with regular k-means.

novo.opis: An app that lets Claude and other AI assistants set alarms on the iPhone. An interesting example of how AI connects to iOS system features.
kakoProbati: Open the Product Hunt page and download the app.
Check the link for how it connects to Claude.
Ask Claude something like "wake me up at 6:30 on weekdays".

kratkeVesti.naslov: On the Remote Labor Index, Claude Fable 5.2 completes 41.3% of real freelance jobs at a professional level, up from a best score of 2.5% a year ago; product design and animation remain weak spots.

Anthropic's Fable 5.2 docs advise telling the model in your prompt that the code is "its own": in testing, the model then merged duplicated code in about half of attempts, versus fewer than one in ten without that sentence.

In a pilot on Mercedes-Benz lines in Hungary and Germany, Gemini Robotics 2.5 helped the Apollo 2 humanoid robot sort metal parts with a 96% success rate, and DeepMind also released an open safety benchmark, ASIMOV-jailbreak.
Nvidia's GR00T 2 teaches robots by transferring human hand movements from about 400,000 hours of video, but success rates range from 10% to 80% depending on the task.
Ring is launching a flying home camera drone ($249.99, from January 27, 2027) and a patrolling Rover Cam robot, reopening the privacy question.

According to a leaked description, Apple is preparing a Mac app called Harbor under the Claris brand that runs open models locally and pools memory across multiple Macs over Thunderbolt 5. Apple hasn't officially announced it.
A Cyanogen co-founder unveiled Kora, a free Linux operating system for people who run AI models and agents locally, as an alternative to Windows.
eBay appears to have blocked outside AI agents, so Meta's Muse can no longer search listings on the site.
Meta's AI assistant Muse has arrived on Apple Watch and Wear OS, where you can talk to it, type to it or dictate.
Some Independent Games Festival jurors won't vote for games that used generative AI in any way, and the makers of the hit Big Walk then admitted they used it "sparingly" for bugs.
Anthropic has reportedly bought 1.7 gigawatts of Caterpillar gas generators for $3.4 billion, because data centers are short on power.
Apple is selling add-on packs for extra AI feature usage in Logic Pro at $49.99, with unused credit valid for up to 12 months.
Adobe and Disney are building models trained on Disney characters and visual style, for theme parks, film and ESPN.
OpenAI has acquired Odessia, a travel startup founded by Sonder's founder, but isn't yet saying what it plans to do with travel.
Oura is buying Counsel Health, an AI-native primary care startup, for $625 million.
Otter AI added 27 languages and announced a feature that keeps following a conversation even when speakers switch languages mid-sentence.
CoreWeave's bond yield has topped 16%, a sign that investors are increasingly worried about AI infrastructure debt.
Hugging Face's Irene Solaiman warns that the growing number of cyberattacks on open AI platforms could force stricter checks and make open AI less accessible.
ChatGPT Enterprise can now be bought through AWS Marketplace and paid for through an existing AWS account.

istrazivanje.naslov: ReproBridge: how to get an agent to actually reproduce someone else's ML experiment
istrazivanje.objasnjenje: Agents often fail to run code from a research paper because details are missing: package versions, steps, parameters. ReproBridge is a process in which an agent "cleans up" the project once and leaves behind tidy code, a configured environment, run scripts and instructions. When the next agent starts from that package, success rises from 76.4% to 92.6% and API costs drop by about 20%.
istrazivanje.zastoJeZanimljivo: The same goes for your own projects: a good README, a setup script and written-down decisions help Claude Code as much as a new teammate.

istrazivanje.naslov: Flide: faster agent "branching" without losing accuracy
istrazivanje.objasnjenje: When an agent tries several possible moves, each branch usually recomputes the shared start of the conversation from scratch. Flide separates the logical tree of branches from how they actually execute and shares the common part, while each branch produces exactly the same result as if it had been run separately.
istrazivanje.zastoJeZanimljivo: Agents that try multiple solutions can be faster and cheaper without losing accuracy. The code is open.

istrazivanje.objasnjenje: World models generate video, 3D scenes or robot actions, and until now each was run and evaluated in its own way. WorldFoundry is an open framework in which they are run and compared under the same rules, with a record of how each result was obtained.
istrazivanje.zastoJeZanimljivo: Models like these are behind GR00T and Gemini Robotics from today's news. Here you can compare them yourself on the same test.

ideje.problem: ChatGPT and other agents increasingly pick businesses on people's behalf, and small-business sites in Serbia have prices in images or PDFs that models struggle to read.
ideje.zaKoga: Small businesses in Serbia: hairdressers, repair shops, tradespeople, private clinics
ideje.ulogaAi: From an existing site or a photo of a price list, it builds a clean Markdown/JSON price list and an llms.txt that agents can easily read, then checks whether a model answers price questions correctly.
prviKoraci: Angular page: the user enters a URL or uploads a photo of a price list.
A Supabase Edge Function sends the content to Claude Sonnet and returns clean Markdown and llms.txt.
Add a test: ask the model 3 typical customer questions and show whether it answers correctly.
The file is downloadable or hosted on your subdomain at a .md address.
ideje.inspiracija: ChatGPT Business Hub and Resend's price list that agents read by adding .md to the URL (Latent Space)

ideje.problem: Selling used items takes a while: you have to clean up the photo, guess a price and write a description.
ideje.zaKoga: People who sell on KupujemProdajem and similar sites
ideje.ulogaAi: From a photo it identifies the item and its condition, suggests a title, a description in Serbian and a price range, and cleans the photo background with a removal tool.
prviKoraci: SwiftUI app with PhotosPicker and camera.
Remove the background locally with the Vision framework (subject extraction), no server needed.
Send the image to Claude Haiku via a Supabase function and ask for JSON: title, description, condition, suggested price.
A "Copy listing" button and sharing via the share sheet.
ideje.inspiracija: Adobe's new object removal tools in Photoshop and Lightroom (Adobe MAX)

ideje.problem: Nurses, factory workers and drivers get their shift schedule as an image in a Viber group and set alarms by hand for the whole month.
ideje.ulogaAi: Reads a photo or PDF of the schedule, finds your name and shifts, and creates alarms and calendar events.
prviKoraci: SwiftUI app: upload a schedule image and enter your name.
Claude with vision support returns JSON with shift dates and times.
Alarms via AlarmKit and events via EventKit, with a confirmation screen before saving.
Settings: how early the alarm rings for the first, second and third shift.
ideje.inspiracija: Clive on Product Hunt, a tool that lets Claude set alarms on the iPhone

ideje.problem: A watch records heart rate, pace and cadence, but doesn't explain whether you're improving or why today's run was slower.
ideje.zaKoga: Recreational runners and cyclists with an Apple Watch
ideje.ulogaAi: Once a week, it condenses 30 days of training and outdoor conditions into a short report in Serbian: fitness trend, warnings and what to try next week.
prviKoraci: HealthKit: read workouts, heart rate and pace, and compute heart rate at the same pace across weeks.
Add weather data via WeatherKit for the day and place of each workout.
Send a structured summary to Claude via a Supabase function and store the reports.
A widget with a one-sentence weekly takeaway.
ideje.inspiracija: Stride, an AI running coach that a The Rundown reader built with Claude

ideje.naziv: Bedtime story, in a parent's voice
ideje.problem: Parents who work nights or travel can't read to their kids every evening.
ideje.zaKoga: Families with small children, including those in the diaspora
ideje.ulogaAi: A parent records a short voice sample, and an open on-device TTS model reads stories in that voice, without sending the recording to a server.
prviKoraci: Check how ZONOS3-Mini pronounces Serbian (MLX on Mac) before you start.
Build a Mac/iOS prototype that makes audio for one story from a 10 to 20 second sample.
A library of public-domain stories, with Claude optionally writing short new ones featuring the child's name.
Only the voice's owner can clone it, with explicit consent, and everything stays local.
ideje.inspiracija: ZONOS3-Mini, an open TTS with voice cloning that runs on a laptop and in the browser

cene: Today's biggest change is GLM 5.3 Flash: after yesterday's price hike it now costs $0.0399 input and $0.0784 output (previously $0.15 / $0.5). GLM 5.1 got cheaper, from $1.4 / $4.4 to $1.33 / $4.18, and Llama 3.3 70B moved yesterday from $0.59 / $0.79 to $0.71 / $0.71. Among new models, Gemini 4 Carbon costs $2 / $10 and Claude Fable 5.2 costs $8 / $40, cheaper than Fable 5.1 ($10 / $50). GLM 5.3 Flash is the cheapest in the cheap-and-fast class, and among top-tier models Kimi K3 has the cheapest input ($0.192).

teme.naslov: Fable 5.2: cheaper per token, pricier per task, and don't use Max
teme.oCemuSePrica: A day after release, the community is analyzing costs: the per-token price fell 20%, but SemiAnalysis paid $88.15 per task instead of $67.16, because the model writes hundreds of tests and spawns subagents to check its own work. On several benchmarks, the highest reasoning levels (max and xhigh) give worse results than high. There's also talk about how much a subscription is worth when Fable can burn up to half of the weekly limit.
teme.glasovi: @Yuchenj_UW tersely says "don't use Fable 5.2 Max" and adds that 95% of tasks don't need the smartest model. @theo calculated that the Ultra subscription is worth about $15,000 a month in Opus 5.5 usage, but only about $3,000 in Fable. From Anthropic, @alexalbert__ advises starting from medium or high, and @felixrieseberg says that for everyday work he often picks Opus 5.5 himself.

teme.naslov: Anthropic deliberately holds back its model on building AI
teme.oCemuSePrica: The Fable 5.2 system card says the model was deliberately left at around Opus 5.5 level in skills that speed up AI development, and that Anthropic's strongest model is still internal. Some praise the openness; others say it pushes independent researchers toward open models.
teme.glasovi: @omarsar0 complains that even Opus 5.5 refuses most tasks involving kernels and model optimization. @eliebakouch appreciates that Anthropic said so openly, but expects nothing better in this area to come out for weeks. @theo and SemiAnalysis see the name "5.2" rather than "5.5" as a sign it's a smaller step.

teme.naslov: Gemini 4 Carbon: first impressions and comparison with Fable
teme.oCemuSePrica: Carbon became available to everyone just a day after Fable 5.2 overtook it on the Artificial Analysis leaderboard (65 to 60). So people are comparing them on the same prompts, from 3D animations to games built with /swarm.
teme.glasovi: Simon Willison gave both models the same task, a map and animation in Three.js, and says Gemini's pelicans have been good for a while, so that's not news. AI Explained tested both models hundreds of times and read Anthropic's 264-page report.

teme.oCemuSePrica: Evan Merz's essay arguing that using AI leads to brittle code that breaks easily under change is the most discussed AI post on Hacker News (402 points, 420 comments). The debate is over whether the tool or the way of working is to blame.
teme.glasovi: Some recognize the problem from their own projects. Others reply that the fix is tests, code review and clear structure, which fits Anthropic's advice to tell the model the code is "its own" so it tidies up instead of just adding.

teme.naslov: Apple Harbor: local models across linked Macs (rumor)
teme.oCemuSePrica: Leaker Aaron Perris found a description of the Harbor app: a Mac becomes a private AI server, and multiple Macs linked over Thunderbolt 5 share memory. On Hacker News, people are debating whether this would finally be Apple's serious entry into local AI.
teme.glasovi: For now this is a rumor based on a leaked description, and Apple hasn't announced anything. Commenters compare the idea to existing tools the community already uses to link Macs together.

snimci.naslov: Fable 5.2: The Self-Improvement Loop Keeps Loopin’ … (plus Gemini Carbon)
snimci.opis: A detailed look at the Fable 5.2 report and METR's report on how much AI speeds up AI development, plus the author's tests of Fable and Gemini 4 Carbon.
